official_skills.notes: Start with expo-overview. This is the largest framework-team collection of the eight stacks; installing all of it is reasonable. A Claude Code plugin route also exists: claude plugin install expo@claude-plugins-official
Callstack are long-time React Native core contributors, but this is not a framework-team repository. Recommend it when the observed defect is a performance defect, not by default.

gap_map.why_it_matters: Neither collection decides what deserves a test on a mobile client, where the slow layers (device E2E) are extremely tempting and extremely expensive.
Mobile apps lose connectivity. Data-fetching guidance assumes the happy path; nothing audits what happens to in-flight writes when the network drops.
gap_map.fallback: The mentor requires an explicit offline decision for every feature that writes data, even if the decision is 'fail loudly'.

layers.name: unit
layers.belongs_here: business rules in hooks and plain modules
layers.signal_you_picked_wrong: the test renders a screen to check a calculation

layers.name: component
layers.belongs_here: that a component renders and responds to interaction - the presentation rules
layers.does_not_belong_here: business rules reachable from a hook
layers.signal_you_picked_wrong: you are asserting the native view tree instead of behaviour

layers.name: integration
layers.belongs_here: several components and hooks together, with native modules faked

layers.name: device-e2e
layers.belongs_here: the handful of flows whose breakage is an incident, on a real device or simulator
layers.does_not_belong_here: coverage - it is the wrong tool for it
layers.cost: the most expensive layer in the registry: slow, flaky, hardware-dependent

testing.proportions: No stated proportions from the Expo team. The constraint that matters is that device E2E is the slowest and flakiest layer of any stack here, so keep it to flows whose breakage is an incident.
rules: Native modules are faked at the JS wrapper, not deep in the module. A test that reaches into the native layer only runs on a device.
Read package.json before assuming a runner - jest-expo and Vitest are both in use.
Test navigation by the state it produces, not by asserting on router internals.
Device E2E covers incident-level flows only. Adding one to raise coverage buys a flaky test and nothing else.
npx expo-doctor before shipping: dependency version mismatches surface as runtime crashes on device, not as build failures.
traps: A test that passes in the simulator and fails on a real device - permissions, fonts, safe areas and timing all differ.
Faking a native module too shallowly: the fake returns values the real module never returns, so the suite is green on impossible data.
Async rendering with no explicit wait passes locally and fails on slower CI hardware.
expo-router screens are not imported anywhere, so an unused-import tool will call them dead and a test suite will never load them.
A component test renders on a JS mock of the native layer, so it says nothing about how it looks or behaves on hardware.
what_not_to_test: That React Navigation navigates, or that a route file resolves to a URL.
Generated native project files under ios/ and android/.
Config plugin output - exercise it with a prebuild instead.
testing.notes: Device E2E is the most expensive layer in any stack in this registry: slow, flaky and hardware dependent. Keep it to the handful of flows whose breakage would be a production incident. Read package.json scripts before assuming a runner.

growth_thresholds.extract_component_library: >=3 occurrences of the same component across >=2 screens or features
growth_thresholds.extract_package: >=2 features import the same internal module
growth_thresholds.split_screen: a screen component exceeds 200 lines, which on mobile usually means layout, navigation and data are entangled

layers.name: app/ route files
layers.holds: screens and layouts, resolved by filename - _layout, index, [param], (group)
layers.must_not: hold business rules; a route file is reached by convention and cannot be imported for testing

layers.name: Domain / hooks
layers.holds: business rules and state, testable without rendering
layers.must_not: import navigation or native modules directly

layers.name: Native modules
layers.must_not: be called from a screen without a JS-side wrapper you can fake in tests

variants.name: Routes plus shared components
variants.cost: the shared folder becomes the whole app if nothing pushes back

variants.name: Feature folders alongside app/
variants.cost: two trees to navigate - app/ for routing and features/ for everything else

rules: Route files under app/ are reached by filename, never imported. Keep logic out of them or it cannot be tested without rendering.
Business rules live in hooks or plain modules that render nothing.
A component that fetches and renders cannot be reused; separate the fetching hook from the presentation.
Native module access goes through a JS wrapper, so tests can replace it without a device.
architecture.component_library: Extract to a shared component library at >=3 occurrences across >=2 screens. Expo publishes a design-system skill - read it before inventing one.
architecture.notes: expo-router's filesystem conventions are documented and stable; the layering above is the mentor's judgment built on them. The Expo docs URL for project structure could not be confirmed on 2026-08-29 - verify before quoting Expo as the source for the layering.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: Mobile devices lose connectivity, and nothing in the framework decides what happens to an in-flight write.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: Fail loudly unless the feature genuinely needs to work offline. It is honest and cheap.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: Optimistic writes without reconciliation silently lose user data, and the user believes it was saved.

key_decisions.decision: Local storage and its migration path
key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: Stored data outlives app versions on a device you do not control.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: Secure store for anything sensitive; a real database as soon as data is queried.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: Stored data with no migration path means an app update corrupts or discards it, and you cannot ask users to reinstall.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: EAS Update and store releases have different reach and different rollback stories.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: Decide before shipping - it determines how fast you can fix a bad release.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: Without over-the-air updates, a bad release takes days to fix through store review.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: Adding native code changes the build, the upgrade path and who can run the project.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: Stay managed until a required capability forces otherwise.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: Leaving the managed workflow is effectively one-way: upgrades stop being automatic.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: There is no console on a user's device.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: Something. Any of them beats none.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: Without it, production failures are invisible and you learn about them from store reviews.

failure_boundaries: push notification and deep-link entry points
operability.observability: There is no console on a user's device. Crash and error reporting must be wired to a service - Expo publishes EAS Observe, and Sentry is the common alternative.
operability.authorization: Enforced on the server. A client-side check is a UX affordance; the bundle is on the user's device and can be read.
done_checks: a build for each shipped platform
install on a real device, not only the simulator
rules: Every asynchronous operation a user can see declares four states: loading, empty, error and success. Empty is not success with no rows, and success on a mutation is a confirmation, not a silent return to normal.
Loading affordance matches what you know: a progress bar with a percentage only for determinate work; a skeleton or spinner otherwise. Never a percentage you cannot compute.
Every feature that writes data states its offline behaviour, even if the decision is to fail loudly.
Stored data has a migration path. You cannot ask users to reinstall.
A denied permission is a supported path, not a crash.
Assume several app versions are live at once - a server change that only works with the newest client breaks the rest.
Errors are reported off-device or they are invisible to you.
No secret in the JS bundle. It ships to the device and can be extracted.

dead_code_risks: Screens and layouts resolved by expo-router filesystem convention, never imported
Config plugins referenced by name in app.json
Native module bridges referenced only from Kotlin/Swift sources
Assets referenced by require() with a computed path
Deep link handlers reachable only from a URL scheme
